# BOARD — the numbered items, enumerated

`ROADMAP.md` references numbered work items everywhere (`board #121`,
`roadmap #43`, `#152`) and **has never listed them**. Reconstructing the board
meant grepping 8,000 lines and reading each hit's surrounding paragraph to find
out whether the number was a work item at all. This file is that list.

It is **hand-maintained** — unlike `rungs/INDEX.md`, there is no header block to
generate it from. Adding a board item means adding a row here **in the same
commit** that mints the number.

---

## Conventions

**The status field and the payoff field are separate, on purpose.** §9.16.1
records what happens when a board's payoff field and its outcome field are the
same field, and #149 is the live instance: its *conversion* was declined while
the *item* stayed open at 356. A board with one column gets that wrong. So:

| status | means |
|---|---|
| **OPEN** | live work. May carry a re-priced number from a lane that measured it and declined to build it. |
| **DONE** | shipped, with the differential behind it. |
| **DECLINED** | measured, deliberately **not** built, with a number attached. The measurement is the deliverable. A declined item is not a failed one. |
| **REFUTED** | the claim was tested and is **false**. The most valuable rows here. |
| **PARTIAL** | some of it shipped; the rest is named. A PARTIAL row lives in the section its dominant half earns — #35 sits under Open (the unshipped rest is the live work), #135 under Done (the measurement is finished; what it failed to ship is named in the row). |
| **UNCLEAR** | the prose does not support a status. Not a guess — a flag that someone must read the bytes. |

**Numbers are never reused and never renumbered.** Every `#N` in `ROADMAP.md` is
a permanent reference into 8,000 lines of prose that will not be rewritten.

### A CODEGEN PRICE CARRIES ITS PROVENANCE, OR IT IS A HAND-COUNT

**Added 2026-08-08 by lane `w-column`, board #1476.** Board **#1464** established
that the frontier ladder instrument has no codegen column and never had one, so
**every codegen number this board has ever published was produced by a human
reading an obj beside an IL body** — #1105's `>= 15` and `>= 21`, #1418's 776
bytes and `>= 8` clauses, #770's eleven-not-eight, #483/#506/#827's seventeen.
Those numbers are not wrong and are not deprecated. What they are is a different
*kind* of number from a scan reading, and until this convention existed nothing
in a row's text said which kind it was.

So a codegen price in the *worth* column now carries one of two tags:

| tag | means |
|---|---|
| **HAND-COUNT** | a person enumerated refusals, clauses or bytes by reading the obj and the IL. Reproducible only by repeating the reading; **not** re-derived by any scan, so it does not move when the tree does and can go stale silently. |
| **INSTRUMENT** | a key a scan prints. Names the key, so a successor can re-read it at their own tree. |

**The tag is on the number, not on the row** — a row may carry both, and #1474 is
the instance. An untagged codegen number in a row written before this date is a
HAND-COUNT by default; that is what #1464 proved and it needs no per-row edit to
be true.

**There is exactly one INSTRUMENT codegen number on the frontier today and it is
`1`** (#1474). That is not an argument for distrusting the hand-counts — they are
the only numbers that exist for the other 48 functions, because the instrument
structurally cannot see behind a reader refusal. It is an argument for never
quoting a hand-count and a scan reading in the same sum.

**Checked, not asserted**: `scripts/board_audit.sh` lists every `#N` in
`ROADMAP.md` with no row here, suppressing the two known non-item series by an
explicit printed list rather than silently. It also resolves every section
anchor in this file (`R:§x` etc.) against a real heading in its target document,
lists any raw line-number anchor as drift waiting to happen, and lists every
board number that a `ROADMAP.md` **heading** names in a section no row of that
number cites — the mechanized form of the 2026-08-02 staleness defect, where
§10.11/§10.13 re-measured #152 and nothing forced the row to notice. `--check`
self-tests all of it without a toolchain, and every check is mutation-tested
(see the script header). Coverage at 2026-08-04, after the `w-book4` mint and **read off a run of the
script rather than off the previous sentence**:
**177 board numbers, 81 cited, 0 uncovered**, 0 unresolved anchors, 0 raw
line-number anchors, 0 rows behind the prose. (It read **148 / 81 / 0** after the
`w-book3` mint, and **50 / 55 / 0** at `a091e37`.)

**The citation count did not move — 81 before the mint and 81 after — and that is
correct rather than a defect.** `ROADMAP.md` is 8k lines of *dated session
history* and none of these 29 numbers existed when its last section was written,
so a new row cannot be cited there until somebody writes prose that cites it.
**The gap between 177 rows and 81 cited is not "96 uncovered items"** — the audit
prints `CITED BUT NOT ON THE BOARD` and that is the direction that matters; the
reverse direction is the board doing its job.

### The 2026-08-01 collision — six numbers carry two meanings each

Two lanes running concurrently (`w-eh` and `w-rerank`) both allocated **143, 144,
145, 146** on the same day, for eight different items; `w-arms` and
`w-emitset`/`w-vgl` did the same to **151** and **152**. `w-eh` records *why*:
its items were "kept out of `ROADMAP.md` on purpose" while the coordinator landed
§9.14 serially — so neither lane could see the other's allocation.

Downstream prose now cites **both senses without disambiguating**. Both are kept
below, suffixed by their minting lane. Renumbering them would silently break
whichever citations meant the other sense.

**The rule that prevents the next one: mint the number by adding the row here
first.** A number that exists only inside a worktree is a number two lanes can
allocate at once.

**Which sense a bare `#N` means by default** — measured over every `ROADMAP.md`
citation, 2026-08-02. For five of the six numbers one sense dominates
completely: outside the minority sense's own minting list, downstream prose uses
the dominant sense every single time. A reader hitting a bare citation should
assume the default below; the minority sense never escapes its minting section.

| bare | default sense | citations | the other sense appears ONLY at |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#143` | *w-rerank*: `…recv-load-then-off-add-more` | 9 of 10 (§9.17 throughout, §10.1, §10.6) | R:§9.15.6 (`__catchsym$F$k`) |
| `#144` | *w-rerank*: "residue 0 is not a control" — cited as that principle | 7 of 9 (§9.17.1, §9.17.8, §9.18.1, §9.20.3, §9.20.6, §9.20.12, §10.11) | R:§9.15.6 (`nIPMapEntries`) |
| `#145` | *w-rerank*: the validator rule | §9.16.3, §9.18.2, two preregs | R:§9.15.6 (`bind.rs:84`; R:§9.20.4 settles that item without using the number) |

The board's `<sub>lane</sub>` suffixes remain the *unambiguous* form; this table

### The 2026-08-04 collision — FOUR lanes all started at `#183`, and it cost nothing

`w-front`, `w-fifth`, `w-bss2` and `w-cfg` each finished the same session with a
proposed row list beginning at **`#183`**, the number this file advertised as
free. None of them wrote to this file, which is the rule working: the collision
was **visible at the funnel and resolved once**, instead of four lanes minting
four `#183`s the way 2026-08-01 minted two `#143`–`#146`s. Resolved by lane
`w-book` (R:§10.23), in this order:

1. **Strike duplicates before ordering anything.** Three of the ten proposals
   already had rows, so they were never candidates for a number: w-fifth's
   `??__F` row is **#180**; w-bss2's "writer scoped to ≤ 2 objects" is a *scope*
   for **#174**, which its own text says it supersedes; w-front's
   "`fn_gate_refusals` == 0" is a re-measurement of **#47**/**#44**. Two more of
   w-front's are not units of work at all. That deflated ten proposals to five
   new numbers and most of the contention with them.
2. **Where two landed records name numbers, prefer the assignment that needs no
   edit to either document.** `OBJ_DATA_BSS_SHAPE.md` §9 (w-bss2) named
   183–186; `CFG_SHAPE.md` §9 (w-cfg) named 186–194 and reasoned explicitly that
   "w-front proposed 183–185, so the next free number is 186". Striking w-bss2's
   writer row freed **185**, so w-bss2's fourth item moved 186 → **185** and
   w-cfg's nine landed **exactly** as its document writes them. One number moved,
   in the lane whose duplicate caused the gap; **no lane's frozen text was
   rewritten**.
3. **A number is not the only way to record a finding.** w-front's headline is a
   *property of the frontier*, not a unit of work, so it took the un-numbered
   `—` row form this board already uses for "the wall does not decompose into
   items".

**One redirect, so the frozen records stay readable**: `w-bss2`'s rung and
`OBJ_DATA_BSS_SHAPE.md` §9 both say *"#186 — census `.tls$`"*. It is **#185**.
Its other two numbers (183, 184) are as written.

**A false alarm worth keeping, because acting on it would have destroyed an
unrelated row.** w-bss2's rung reports that *"#166/#178 should be re-scoped or
struck"*. **#166 is not implicated.** The lane's §9 keeps its pre-mint bullet
list under the old numbers with a `#162 → #174 … #166 → #178` redirect at its
head, so *"#166"* there is **#178's own former number** — one item cited under
both spellings, not two items. Board **#166** is w-map's "retarget the *split*
concept to stripped x86 PE" and has nothing to do with `.bss`. See #178.

### #194's document audit — the list

Driving the audit is not doing it: **each entry below belongs to its document's
owner**, and no derivation of another lane's has been rewritten here. What this
list settles is *which documents need an owner to look* and *what they should
look for*.

**The mechanism, re-measured rather than inherited** (lane `w-book2`, four
tracked fixtures — `add3`, `w5_chain`, `w17_ptr_operand`, `il_convert_scalar` —
each captured twice through the *fixed* `capture --flags-file`, at `/Ox /GS- /c`
and `/O1 /GS- /c`, and compared byte for byte):

| file | `/Ox` vs `/O1` |
|---|---|
| `.gl` | **byte-identical**, 4 of 4 fixtures |
| `.sy` | **byte-identical**, 4 of 4 |
| `.in` | **byte-identical**, 4 of 4 |
| `.db` | **byte-identical**, 4 of 4 |
| `.ex` | same length; differs in **4 / 4 / 23 / 19** bytes |

**And every differing byte is one byte, at the same position, inside a
`4F 1F 80 05 00 <a0\|20> 00 00` per-function optimization word — `a0` at `/Ox`,
`20` at `/O1`, with nothing else in the bundle moving at all.** That both
confirms and **sharpens** the recorded mechanism, and the sharpening matters for
the audit: the count is **one byte per `4F 1F` function segment**, so it is 4 on
`add3` and 23 on `w17_ptr_operand`. *"The seven per-function optimization
words"* is `pa.cpp`'s segment count, not a universal 7 — `CFG_SHAPE.md` §10.1
says *"one per function"* and is right; the paraphrase in the row above reads as
a constant and is not.

**The criterion this gives an auditor**, and it is sharper than "was it captured
before `6a33b4d`": a claim is at risk **only** if its derivation reads the *value*
of a per-function opt word. Reading `.gl`, `.sy`, `.in` or `.db` is moot.
*Splitting* `.ex` on `4F 1F` or `4C 4F 11` is also moot — the marker bytes are
identical and only the payload byte moves.

| document | the claim at risk | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `CFG_SHAPE.md` §10.1 and throughout | every `.ex` byte it quotes | **MOOT — cleared by its own control, already recorded.** Captured via `census --flags-file`; §10.1 *is* the two-arm comparison. |
| `OBJ_DATA_BSS_SHAPE.md` §5.6–§5.8 | the `.gl` data records behind Rules A1/A2/T1 | **MOOT on the numbers** — `.gl` is byte-identical, and the lane never used the CLI (`cap.py`). Already recorded at §11. |
| `OBJ_DATA_BSS_SHAPE.md` **§5.2** | *"Measured, **at workload flags**, with the `.gl` read directly out of the captured IL (`c2rs capture --keep-il`)"* | **FLAGGED FOR ITS OWNER — provenance, not numbers.** `c2rs capture` **could not take workload flags** when that line was written, so the sentence cannot be true as spelled; §11 names `glorder.py` as the actual instrument. The *claim* is moot (it reads `.gl` record order, byte-identical either way) but the *provenance line* is wrong and only its owner should correct it. **Do not "fix" it by deleting the parenthetical** — which of the two halves is wrong is the question. |
| `ROADMAP.md` §10.11 (the `TomCryptLicense`/`ZlibLicense` table) | *"the four bytes after `4F 1F 80`" = `0x00200005`* | **MOOT, and self-verifying.** It reads an opt-word value — but the value it reports is `OPT_WORD_O1`, which a `/Ox` capture **cannot** produce. The number is its own evidence that the instrument was the workload path. |
| `OPT_MODE.md` (the whole flag→word table) | `/Ox` `00a00005` vs `/O1` `00200005`, and every `#pragma optimize` row | **MOOT.** Its instrument is `c2rs gap --flags-file` (§4.0), which always honoured flags — and the table *varies* with the flag, which a dropped-flag path cannot do. §3's *"captured with the default `/Ox /GS- /c`"* is an honest statement of a default, which is a different thing from a flag accepted and discarded. |
| `IL_STORE_LEAF.md` §(repro) | the 87-TU sub-shape survey via `census <tu> --keep-il` with no `--flags-file` | **MOOT.** `census` always parsed `--flags-file` correctly, so this is a *chosen default*, not a dropped flag; and the survey re-splits `.ex` on the `LO` anchor, whose marker bytes do not move. Its published numerators come from `gap --flags-file`. |
| every other `docs/*.md` using `census … --keep-il` (≈20 files: `IL_STMT_LAYER`, `IL_CALL_IN_EXPR`, `IL_EXPR_LAYER`, `IL_CAST_CONVERT`, `IL_CALL_GRAMMAR`, `IL_INTRINSIC_CALL`, `IL_SY_LOCALS`, `IL_LOAD_TYPES`, `OPERATOR_GRANTS`, `CODEGEN_*`, `GAPS.md`, …) | their quoted IL byte strings | **MOOT — out of scope by construction.** `cmd_census` has parsed its options with a refusing loop the whole time; **`c2rs capture` is the only command that ever dropped a flag.** Grepped, not assumed: `c2rs capture` occurs in exactly 8 files under `docs/`, and 5 of those are the row, the pointer, the finder and two prose mentions. |
| `rungs/_2026-08-01-w-vgl-prereg.md` §(instrument hygiene) | *"Both sides of any comparison are captured the same way, through the same `c2rs capture`"* | **MOOT, and the reasoning still holds.** It registers that both arms use one path — which is exactly the property the bug preserved. A dropped flag makes two arms *identical*, and identical is what this clause asked for. |
| `README.md` §(scratch), `ROADMAP.md` §(P2 plan sketch) | — | **NO CLAIM.** Prose describing regenerability and a procedure. Closed. |

**Nothing was found that publishes a number derived from a wrongly-flagged opt
word.** That is a *negative result over the documents that were grepped*, not a
proof of absence — per trap 5, the check that would have shown it is the byte
comparison above, and it was run.

### #231's sweep — every subcommand's option parse, before the seam

Derived from `main.rs`'s dispatch `match` (26 arms), not from memory. **22 of the
26 carried at least one defect of the class** — the four clean ones are `listing`
and the three group dispatchers. The three that boards #194/#195 named were the
three that happened to surface; **nineteen more were not.**

> **This paragraph read "17 of 26" and "fourteen more" when first written, and
> the commits that landed it say the same.** Recounted from the table below
> rather than from the sentence: 26 rows, 4 marked clean, so 22 carry a defect
> and 19 are new. Left visible rather than silently corrected — a summary
> disagreeing with the table under it is the staleness class this board's own
> coverage line was caught by one commit earlier, and the fix in both cases is
> the same: **derive the count from the artifact, never from the previous
> sentence.** The count here is reproducible by
> `grep '^| \`' docs/BOARD.md` over this table.

The class boundary, stated so the 22 is checkable: a row counts if an argument
was **accepted and then not acted on as written** — scanned past, parsed into a
variable some path ignores, or turned into a default because its value did not
parse. `listing-scan` is the weakest member and is counted: it *refused* a bad
`--jobs` but with **no message at all**, so the user learns only that something
was wrong.

Columns: **parse** = how options were found · **order** = where
`located()` sat relative to validation · **drop** = an argument accepted and then
not consumed · **num** = a bad number silently becoming the default.

| subcommand | parse | order | drop | num | the specific defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `capture` | loop | ok | **yes** | — | `--cwd` consumed only on the `--flags-file` path |
| `compile` | **scan** | **locate-first** | **yes** | — | board #195; `--flag` accepted and dropped |
| `census` | loop | **locate-first** | **yes** | — | `--flags-file` read *after* `located()`; no empty-profile refusal; no profile echo; `--cwd` dropped |
| `selftest` | none | **locate-first** | **yes** | — | `rest` mapped wholesale to fixture paths, so `--flags-file f` became two "fixtures" |
| `replay` | none | ok | **yes** | — | `rest[1..]` discarded without a word |
| `replay-c1` | none | ok | **yes** | — | as `replay` |
| `diff` | none | ok | **yes** | — | as `replay`; *"`diff` does not take `--flags-file`"* meant "accepts and ignores it" |
| `bench` | none | **locate-first** | **yes** | — | dispatched as `cmd_bench()` — arguments dropped **by the dispatcher**, above any handler that could refuse them |
| `perf` | **scan** | **locate-first** | — | **yes** | `located()` was the first statement |

Two cross-cutting ones with no column of their own: `require_cpp` returned
`rest.first()` verbatim, so a flag-shaped first token became the source path
(`c2rs diff --help` looked for a file called `--help`); and `opt()`'s doc comment
claimed it handled *"a leading positional"*, which it never did — each caller
re-derived positionals ad hoc, and four had a `!starts_with("--")` guard that
three did not.

**Every one of these is now expressed as data** — a `Spec` per subcommand, with
`Arity`, `requires` edges for dangling options, `num` for numbers and `one_of`
for enumerated values — so the next subcommand inherits the refusals instead of
re-earning them.

## Contradictions carried deliberately

These are **not** bookkeeping errors to tidy away. Each is a place where the
prose disagrees with itself, and the disagreement is evidence about how the
project works. Resolving them silently would destroy that.

1. **#143–#146 minted twice, same day, two lanes** (R:§9.15.6 vs R:§9.14.10). Prose
   cites both senses undisambiguated: R:§9.16.3 and two preregs use #145 in the
   *w-rerank* sense; R:§9.20.4 resolves #145 in the *w-eh* sense. **Cause: numbers
   minted inside worktrees.** The fix is this file.
2. **#151/#152 likewise** (`w-arms` vs `w-emitset`/`w-vgl`). All of §9.20 is
   written in the second sense with no acknowledgement the first exists.
3. **#121 reads NOT settled → stands open → still open → settled** (R:§9.15.2
   twice — its heading and its close — then R:§9.15.6, then R:§9.20.4).
   Chronologically consistent; the earlier text was never
   amended. Compounded by R:§9.15: §9.2 and the lane brief attach #121 to **two
   unrelated artifacts**, and both were addressed.
4. **#110's closure is asserted but its registered claim scored MISS** (−3,761,
   R:§9.14.1), with R:§9.14.1 conceding "a ≥90 % drop was never what #110 claimed".
   #110 is never independently declared closed, and §9.11's separate
   `-whole`-suffix corruption (**18,931**) is still live.
5. **#149 is both "DECLINED" (R:§9.19) and "stays open at 356" (R:§9.19.8).**
   Reconcilable — conversion vs item — and it is exactly why this board has two
   fields.
6. **#136's 0.0000 pp is a denominator error term, not a numerator guarantee**
   (R:§9.9.3). Carried here so it is not read as the latter.

> **Two caution notes for whoever audits this block.**
>
> 1. **Verify a mint under TWO patterns, not one.** The strict form
>    `^| \*\*<N>\*\*<sub>` returns a **false absence** on `#3194`, whose row is
>    `| **3194** (OPEN)<sub>w-vocabgap</sub>` — the `(OPEN)` marker sits between
>    the number and the `<sub>`. `w-bind16`'s block records this and `w-section`'s
>    **#3213**-block records the free-number pointer's own reader returning a false
>    absence. **A spent-number check that returns a false absence is exactly what
>    licenses a double-mint**, and `board_audit.sh` counts *duplicates* rather
>    than *absences*, so it cannot catch that direction. Both patterns were run
>    for this block and agree: **`#3214`–`#3217` were free, and are now spent.**
> 2. **A merged-but-unallocated block is invisible to `board_audit.sh`** — it
>    cannot see a row with no number at all, which is how four rows went
>    unallocated this month. These have numbers now.
>
> Appended at the **bottom** (`2026-08-14-irg.md` §8.5's ordering hazard) and is

## `w-fence163` — 2026-08-17, **`#3225`–`#3228` MINTED HERE, BY EXPLICIT COORDINATOR ALLOCATION AND NOT FROM THE POINTER. THE NEXT FREE NUMBER IS `#3234`.**

**THIS BLOCK WAS FIRST MINTED AS `#3218`–`#3221` AND IT COLLIDED.** `w-gatewire`
minted the same four numbers on its own branch, and **both lanes had verified
row-by-row, under both patterns, against a master where neither had landed.**
That is not a check either lane skipped — it is a check that **cannot see an
unmerged peer's mint**, because two branches cannot read each other's
`docs/BOARD.md`. The row-by-row scan is the strongest verification available and
it is **structurally blind in exactly this direction**; `board_audit.sh` is worse
off still, since it counts duplicates only *after* both blocks are on one branch.

**So the pointer mechanism failed twice in one wave**, and the resolution was not
a better read of the pointer: the coordinator **allocated ranges explicitly** —
`#3218`–`#3224` `w-gatewire`, `#3225`–`#3228` this lane, `#3229` upward
`w-mutcensus`. These four numbers were taken from that allocation, **not** from
the next-free pointer, and they were confirmed unheld on master `261d05cb`
before renumbering (`#3225`–`#3228` return 0 under both patterns; `#3218`–`#3224`
resolve to `w-gatewire` and `#3229`–`#3233` to `w-mutcensus`).

## `w-corpushealth` — 2026-08-18, **`#3251`–`#3255` ALLOCATED BY THE COORDINATOR**, not read from the pointer

`docs/rungs/README.md` § "Board numbers are allocated by the coordinator" is
binding; this block was handed to the lane in its dispatch and the next-free
pointer was **not** consulted. Peers `w-calleeguard` and `w-c2map` were in
flight and are blind to this mint by construction.

The lane tests the project owner's hypothesis — *"it's possible that c2-rs fails
on some of our bytes because they are invalid"* — against `../dc3-decomp`'s own
progress signal, read-only. The answer is a **clean negative**, and the two rows
worth reading first are **#3251** (the ceiling) and **#3252** (the floor that
makes the ceiling irrelevant). Rung: `docs/rungs/2026-08-18-corpushealth.md`.

And each worktree mints its own capture-cache generation at its own paths: **19,556 sweep keys + 90,812 cross keys = ~110,000 entries**, order **770 MB**, per worktree, for bytes another worktree already holds | the new state is bounded at **one directory per distinct corpus content** — not per lane, per run or per worktree — and a new generation appears only when `sweep_gen.py` or `sweep.d` changes | rungs/2026-08-18-coldcross.md §6 · `scripts/corpus_dir.sh` header · **#3265**, **#3249** | **A CHANGE THAT ADDS A CACHE HAS TO SAY WHAT BOUNDS IT, AND THIS ONE'S ANSWER IS THAT IT IS A NET REMOVAL.** A repeat corpus mints **zero** new capture-cache entries and zero new 83 MB copies. It is also safe to garbage-collect by hand in a way `work/capture-cache` is not: a generation is immutable and regenerable in 0.65 s, and deleting one mid-run degrades to a **loud, cold, correct** fallback rather than a wrong verdict — because the resolver re-verifies the whole corpus by byte compare on every run |
| **3286**<sub>w-coldcross</sub> | **NEITHER GENERATED GATE ROW EVER VERIFIED ITS OWN CORPUS — `count > 0` WAS THE ENTIRE CHECK, AND IT IS THE CHECK THE SHARED DIRECTORY COULD NOT SHIP WITHOUT** | **CLOSED, and the closure is what made sharing admissible.** Both drivers regenerated their case directory and graded it with no verification beyond `total_cases -eq 0` (itself added only on 2026-08-18, #3264). `resolve_corpus` now regenerates into the run's own private directory and adopts the shared generation **only** if `diff -rq` finds all 19,556 files byte-identical — **1.2 s including the generation** | `gate.sh --selftest` **183 cases, 0 failed** (floor 170 → 183). Ten of the thirteen new arms construct a **wrong** shared generation — short by one case, long by one, tampered by one byte at the same name and count, unwritable root, ungenerable tree — and require a REFUSAL and a cold private fallback | rungs/2026-08-18-coldcross.md §7.1 · `scripts/corpus_dir.sh` · `scripts/gate.sh` `--selftest` | **IT IS THE SECOND INSTANCE IN TWO DAYS, IN THE SAME TWO FILES, OF A CORPUS-SIZED QUANTITY TRUSTED ON A COUNT — AND THE FIRST FIX IS WHAT MADE THE SECOND VISIBLE.** **#3264** found `ls | wc -l` blowing `ARG_MAX` and `0` sitting in a gate row's headline; `w-gateperf` replaced it with a *positively checked* `total_cases -eq 0`, which is strictly better and **is still a count**. A count cannot see a corpus short by one case, long by one, or one byte different at the same name — and the third is the only one that would silently change what the gate grades. **When the thing being checked is a corpus, the check has to be corpus-shaped**; it costs 1.2 s here, which is the whole reason the weaker check survived. **SHARING STATE BETWEEN LANES IS THE CHANGE MOST ABLE TO MAKE ONE LANE'S GATE PASS ON ANOTHER'S EVIDENCE, SO THE PRICE OF ADMISSION IS THAT EVERY WRONG SHARED CORPUS IS REFUSED.** The one-byte tamper arm is the load-bearing one: same names, same count — the only corruption a count-shaped check cannot see, and the only one that would silently change what the gate grades. **And what is shared is only the case SOURCES**, a pure function of the reading lane's own `sweep_gen.py` + `sweep.d` (both in the digest). The port is recompiled and re-run per case per run, the obj compare runs per case per run, the sweep's P0.1 replay runs per case per run, and the cache serves `c2`'s **own** obj keyed over inputs that cannot contain the port |

### A SIXTH ROW, DRAFTED **UNNUMBERED** — the block `#3282`–`#3286` was exhausted at five

`docs/rungs/README.md` § *"Board numbers are allocated by the coordinator"* is
binding, and this lane's allocation is five rows, all spent above. The row below
is the call `w-gateperf` and `w-dataseam` both made one wave earlier: **draft it
unnumbered and ask.** The coordinator asked for it explicitly at rebase time,
having verified the incident independently; it needs one number.

| row | claim | state | evidence | consequence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **3287**<sub>w-coldcross</sub> | **`git add -f` ON A DIRECTORY DEFEATS THE ONE RULE STANDING BETWEEN A SCRATCH TREE AND THE REPOSITORY — AND IT IS REACHED FOR IN ORDER TO KEEP *LEGITIMATE* EVIDENCE** | **HAPPENED, IN THIS LANE, AND WAS DISCARDED RATHER THAN PATCHED OVER.** A commit of contention-lab artifacts used `git add -f work/w-coldcross/contend` and committed **236,616 files, 234,672 of them generated `.cpp` cases**. The `-f` was there for a good reason — `.gitignore` carries `/work`, and every lane's run logs live under `work/`, so the evidence this project asks lanes to commit **cannot be added without it** | discarded by **resetting the branch**, not by a follow-up `git rm --cached`, so the blobs are in no history; the injection and revert commits were **cherry-picked back** so the negative result survived. The retained set is **63 files / 11,628 insertions, largest blob 4,999 lines, ZERO `.cpp`** — verified independently by the coordinator | rungs/2026-08-18-coldcross.md; `work/merge-w-coldcross.txt`; the commit message of `a9406fab` states it in full | **THE MECHANISM IS THAT ONE `.gitignore` EXPRESSES TWO DIFFERENT RULES AND `-f` SILENCES BOTH.** `/work` means *"scratch, not worth committing"* — routinely and correctly overridden. `*.obj`, `*.il`, `_CL_*` mean *"NEVER commit this"* — a hard `CLAUDE.md` prohibition. A `-f` reached for to satisfy the first **suspends the second in the same stroke**, and the operator's intent ("keep my logs") is indistinguishable from the outcome ("commit a corpus"). **The narrow mitigation is to name FILES, never a directory** — `git add -f <dir>` cannot be audited before it runs, `git add -f <dir>/*.log` can. The wider one is that a lab directory under `work/` will contain a full corpus whenever a driver's private-fallback path fires inside it, which is exactly what the contention arms were built to make happen |

THIS IS THE FIRST MEASUREMENT OF WHAT THAT COSTS, AND IT IS NOT THE REGIME THAT ROW'S ADVICE IS CALIBRATED FOR.** #3249 counsels treating any effect under ~10 bodies as *unattributable rather than reporting it* — sound for noise, and useless here: **21 % of the published key surface moved**, from a repository nobody in this lane touched, inside one campaign's wall clock. **The mitigation is one line and it is not in the standing block: read both ends back to back AND ASSERT THE WORKLOAD STAMP IS EQUAL** — `c2rs gap` already prints it on every run (`workload <sha> (clean) <path>`), so the check costs a `diff` of two strings. Without it, a lane that compares its two ends as originally run publishes **82 moved keys** and owes a cause for every one of them; the failure is silent, arrives with a plausible story attached, and is **worse the longer the lane takes** |

**CONFIRMED AT THE FUNNEL, ON A SECOND INSTANCE, BY THE COORDINATOR — AND THE
STORY THAT NEARLY SHIPPED WAS A CORRECTNESS ONE.** Regenerating `STATUS.md` at
`977827d78` moved four rows against the block collected at `571a8d4c3`: `.gl`
name-conflicts **573 → 803 (+230)** while total records moved only **+16**,
row-conflicts +10, nameless flat at 421. `bind.rs:313`'s totality identity
(`records == bound + outside + nameless + row-conflicts + name-conflicts`) then
says **~224 records that used to bind no longer do** — a reach regression in
`w-glattrs`' just-landed `gl.rs` reader (+292/−16), which is the file that
decodes the very field involved. The coordinator registered **0.7 on the
reader** before measuring, on the argument that a workload change moves the
population and the buckets *together* whereas this moved the classification
almost alone.

**REFUTED.** A worktree at the pre-`w-glattrs` commit `e95543cd7`, scanned
against the **same asserted stamp** `49ad7cfd5` (verified clean at both ends,
per this row's own mitigation), reads `1462237` records · `421` nameless ·
`39170` row-conflicts · **`803`** name-conflicts · `fnbyte-exact` **35,886** ·
denominator `162063` · match 26 · mismatch 0 — **identical to master on every
counter**. `w-glattrs` moved the binding accounting by **exactly zero**; all
four rows are the sibling repo.

Two things this adds to the row. **The reasoning was internally valid and still
worthless**: the identity is real, the arithmetic is right, and it was applied
to a delta whose cause was outside the repo — so *soundness of the inference is
not evidence about the premise*, and the stamp check dissolves in five minutes
what an identity argument cannot settle at all. And **the cost is now measured
on a second axis**: the first instance moved a *driver* metric (`fnbyte`), this
one pointed at a **named file and a named regression** in a lane that had
already been merged. A dispatch on that story would have sent a lane to bisect
a reader that never changed a byte of the number it was accused of moving.

This lane's subset is 7 tokens on a body with no call, no branch, no memory reference and no constant, and the two rules carrying the shape of the answer are transcriptions. Naming which rules are derived is the whole difference between a decoder and a lookup table with extra steps |
| **3360**<sub>w-ildecode</sub> | **A PEER LANE'S INSTRUMENT SUBSUMED THIS ONE'S MID-FLIGHT, AND THE RIGHT MOVE WAS TO DELETE MINE — NOT TO MERGE TWO WALKS OVER THE SAME POINTERS** | **DECIDED and RECORDED.** This lane had written and greened its own tap extension: an `OPD` line per tuple carrying three registers via the encoder's own path (`operand+0x1c -> +0x28`), env-gated, with its own neutrality test. `w-restim` landed first with a strictly richer version — an eighth site `after0`, a whole-function walk, and an operand walk over both lists reaching the assigned AND physical registers. Mine was deleted in the rebase resolution, master taken verbatim for `c2host/stagetap.c` and `crates/c2-reference/src/stage.rs`, and the lane's proof rebuilt on theirs | the two paths were then **reconciled rather than assumed compatible**: `sym+0x08 -> +0x1c` (w-restim, `n = r+1`) equals `operand+0x1c -> +0x28` (the encoder) plus one — confirmed by construction, `0x0c` where the obj has `r11`. Net shared-file delta from this lane: **zero lines** in `c2host/` and in `crates/c2-reference/src/stage.rs` | rungs/2026-08-21-w-ildecode.md §5 · **#3352** · **W-STAGETAP-4** · `CLAUDE.md` (worktree protocol) | **WHEN A PEER'S INSTRUMENT SUBSUMES YOURS, THE MERGE HAZARD IS NOT THE TEXTUAL CONFLICT — IT IS THE ONE THAT DOESN'T CONFLICT.** Two operand walks over `tuple+0x28`/`+0x2c` in one tap would have merged cleanly, doubled the payload, and left two register encodings (`n` and `n−1`) in one stream for a later reader to confuse. What this lane kept is the READING — the encoder and its two tables — which is documentation, not instrumentation, and which does not conflict with anything |
